The global economy operates like a high-stakes "debt game" open to any nation willing to play. In this system, debt acts as the essential lubricant required to maximize a country's economic efficiency and productivity. As long as a nation can continuously attract foreign investment, drive domestic production, and maintain affordable repayment terms, the machine keeps running smoothly—under the assumption that future generations or expanding economies will ultimately foot the bill.
However, this delicate balancing act is far more volatile and intricate than it appears on the surface, as a shift in any single variable can stall the entire engine.😕👍
